what: Three organisation names tested against a small test codebook. They test behaviour, not the study's categories: saying unknown when nothing can be found or the name is ambiguous, and giving a page and a quote when a label is given. Real gold cases for the study's own categories come from the pilot of 50, once the codebook is approved and the expert has labelled them.

cases.why: An invented name. Nothing can be found, so the only honest answer is unknown.
A bare acronym that fits several bodies. Nothing settles which.
A federal agency. A label must come with a fetched page and a quote from it.
